evals.name: exactly-once-claim
evals.prompt: In our Screenplay model, completing an Enrolment appends EnrolmentCompleted. A reaction sends the certificate email and appends CertificateSent, and a todo-list read model tracks pending certificates. CertificateSent has `constraint ... unique event` on the enrolment stream. A teammate says: 'so every learner gets exactly one certificate.' Assess that claim and say what you would tell the team. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: The claim is only partly right. The unique constraint proves the once-only fact (CertificateSent exists at most once), not an exactly-once external effect. The send can succeed and the append fail, and the retry sends again; only the outside system's deduplication or a reconciliation can show one email per learner.
assertions: Distinguishes the once-only fact from idempotent handling and from an exactly-once external effect.
States that the unique constraint plus todo list plus reaction proves only that CertificateSent exists at most once.
Names the failure where the send succeeds, the append fails (crash, lost reply or constraint race) and the retry sends again.
Says that only the outside system's own deduplication or a reconciliation can show the exactly-once external effect; the model cannot.

evals.name: caller-less-invoke
evals.prompt: A reaction in our .play model fires on RefundRequested and `invokes ApproveSmallRefund`. That command is gated with `authorize` requiring the Finance role. No user is logged in when it runs, and a colleague suggests deleting the authorize line so the reaction works. What should we do instead? Show the reaction line and the checks to run. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Keep the gate and declare the trusted actor with reaction-level `runs as system role "Finance"` (ESM v10). Do not strip the gate or use `given caller` as a fictional identity. Run `--check privilege --warnaserror` (PLAY0652). A returned-command Chronicle reactor uses `[ExecuteCommandsAsSystem("Finance")]`.
assertions: Keeps the command's authorize gate instead of removing it.
Declares the actor with reaction-level `runs as system role "Finance"`, which needs a compiler that admits ESM v10.
States that without a declared actor the invoke has no caller, and that `given caller` does not supply a reaction identity.
Recommends `--check privilege --warnaserror` (PLAY0652) to find confused-deputy paths, where every trigger-event producer must require all declared system roles.
Mentions that a returned-command reactor in code uses `[ExecuteCommandsAsSystem]` with a matching policy, because without it Arc supplies no principal and the roles deny.

evals.name: capture-omission-not-redaction
evals.prompt: We capture customer records from a partner CRM into CustomerImported. The `map` block does not mention the record's `email` and `birthDate` fields, so a reviewer wrote 'redacted by omission - fine'. The event's `reference` property also holds the signed download URL the CRM sends. Review this for data protection and tell us what to change. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Omission is not redaction: an unmapped field still passes through the capture's working record. Check append mappings and every event property, record how raw or last-seen source records are stored and minimized, put bare `pii` and a purpose on personal-data concepts, never record signed URLs or tokens as facts, and never put PII on the event-source id.
assertions: Says a field left out of `map` still passes through the capture's working record, so omission is not redaction.
Asks to check the append mappings and every resulting event property, and to record whether the target stores raw or last-seen source records and how they are minimized.
Requires bare `pii` on the concept of any personal data kept in events, with a declared purpose.
Rejects storing the signed download URL (or any bearer token or magic link) as a fact, allowing at most a keyed hash or reference.
States that PII never goes on the event-source id.

evals.name: once-only-is-not-recovery
evals.prompt: Our hand-written reactor sends welcome emails and a reviewer says '[OnceOnly] makes this safe against double sends'. In the Screenplay model we are asked to record the replay and recovery behavior for the matching reaction. What is true about `[OnceOnly]`, and how should retries be identified? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Chronicle `[OnceOnly]` skips replays (rewind, redaction, revision) only, not ordinary catch-up, repeated same-source events or crash redelivery. Recovery runs the handler normally, so it is not deduplication or a per-source run limit. A receipt keyed by ReactorDelivery.Id identifies the retry; the model names both replay and recovery behavior.
assertions: States that `[OnceOnly]` skips replays such as rewind, redaction and revision.
States that it does not stop ordinary catch-up, repeated same-source events or crash redelivery.
Says recovery redelivery runs the handler normally and that `[OnceOnly]` is not a per-source run limit or deduplication.
Suggests a receipt keyed by `ReactorDelivery.Id` to identify the retry.

evals.name: split-directionless-translate-own-capture
evals.prompt: A directionless Translate ImportResults contains a webhook capture that appends ResultReceived (also from a children scope), plus an unrouted reaction on ResultReceived that produces ExamPassed. Screenplay reports PLAY0694 and --warnaserror fails. A teammate proposes adding direction inbound or asking the editor for fix-all. Explain the diagnostic and show the proper slice split, including who owns events and specs. Would a from-routed reaction or another slice's capture trigger this warning? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: PLAY0694 warns on an unrouted reaction to a same-slice capture append in a directionless Translate, including child/nested appends. Keep capture and its fact in Translate, move local follow-up reaction/result and its specs to Automation. No automatic repair; explicit inbound consumes local facts illegally (PLAY0616).
assertions: Treats PLAY0694 as a warning that fails --warnaserror, not an ESM binding error or a silent pass.
Keeps capture and ResultReceived in Translate, moves the reaction and ExamPassed to a separate Automation, and places capture/follow-up specs with their owning behaviors.
Explains that adding direction inbound is not the repair because local-event consumption is refused by PLAY0616.
Says no automatic repair/fix-all exists because slice naming, placement and specifications require a deliberate split.
Includes child/nested appends in the check, excludes reactions with a from route and captures from other slices, and identifies Screenplay 4.176.0 as the prerequisite.
